content.comment_body: Hello everyone, INTRO A coworker noticed an issue today that I wanted to share for learning purposes. I'm not seeking a solution, but perhaps someone can identify the cause. BACKGROUND We're preparing for a project using a [product_name] with two I/O expansion modules, giving us 24 inputs and 20 outputs. My colleague was creating the program in [product_name] V8 to include all previously designed circuits. Inputs were referenced, and he moved to configure the outputs. ISSUE Nineteen outputs integrated without problems, but the twentieth output showed up as just "Q" instead of "Q20" in the instruction. Despite several attempts, we couldn't add Q20 to the program. A modified file is attached—I'd be curious to see if others can add all 20 outputs without the trouble we faced. WORKAROUND This appears tied to that specific file. My colleague was able to make a new project where all outputs, including Q20, could be added successfully. --- Any thoughts? w

Hi, Things get stranger: I converted the file to ladder format, and then I could add Q20. Switching back to the previous format made everything work again—you can delete outputs and select all (including Q20) without issue. In another test, after converting formats twice, I ended up with two instances of Q1. Removing one allowed me to add Q20. However, this approach causes confusion in a larger program and disrupts the schematic. I wonder if any parts were edited in ladder format and converted previously? Best regards,

[user_name], Thanks for looking into this and sharing your observations—even if they seem odd. I can confirm my coworker didn't use ladder format at any stage. In our office, it's standard to use only the FBD style with [product_name]. I find it unsettling that teaching at the local college involves encouraging students to use ladder for their projects.
Another curiosity: this diagram has a smaller canvas size than usual. How did you set that up? Was it originally created in an earlier version and then opened in V8?

[user_name], There's an active discussion called: TIPS & TRICKS: [product_name] V8 & [product_name] On page 2, you'll find: [LINK] (Date Code: 11/20/2014, 10:38 PM) WORKING WITH MULTIPLE PAGES IN ONE PROJECT That has the answer to your question. The short version: It's controlled by printer settings. Best regards, w
Interesting—I didn't realize that was an option.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users encountered an uncommon situation where the twentieth output couldn't be added in a project using [product_name] V8 with two I/O expansion cards. The software would display only a generic output label, not the correct designation. Attempts to resolve included switching between diagram formats, which sometimes fixed the issue but could also introduce duplicate elements and confusion in the project structure. The root problem seems related to the specific project file or possibly to migration from earlier software versions, rather than differences in editing styles.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish for all outputs, including the twentieth, to be referenced and configured within [product_name] V8 smoothly, providing a straightforward and dependable programming workflow.
